sovereign_country.strategic_role: 拉美美元金融中枢、私人利益基金会（PIF）与运河船舶登记

applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Panama-United States Trade Promotion Agreement (signed 2007, in force 2012)
Panama-Netherlands Investment Promotion and Protection Agreement (2013)
EU-Central America Association Agreement (multi-party, in force for Panama 2013)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Ley 25 de 12 de junio de 1995 (Private Interest Foundation regime); Ley 23 de 27 de abril de 2015 on AML/CFT, as amended by Ley 70 de 2019, and Decreto Ejecutivo No. 363 de 6 de julio de 2015; Article 21 of Ley 23 imposes mandatory beneficial owner identification and filing of UBO details with the Registro Público de Panamá.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Foundation charter (Escritura de Constitución de Fundación de Interés Privado)
Certificate of initial endowment (Certificación de aporte inicial)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Founder or licensed Panamanian banking/fiduciary institution

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified passport copies and UBO identification evidence of the founder, beneficiaries, and council members
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the country of origin

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all natural persons (founder, council members, beneficiaries and ultimate beneficial owners) against PEP lists, OFAC SDN List, United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, EU consolidated sanctions, and domestic Panamanian regulatory lists issued by the Superintendencia de Bancos and the Unidad de Análisis Financiero. Enhanced due diligence, further source-of-funds disclosure and senior-compliance approval are triggered for any listed or PEP-related relationship.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Público de Panamá – Sección de Fundaciones de Interés Privado (including electronic consultation via the eServicios portal)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The foundation name may be registered in Spanish or a foreign language, must be expressed exclusively in Latin alphabet characters, and must include or be accompanied by the suffix 'Fundación', 'Foundation' or an equivalent abbreviation. A non-Latin-script name requires an apostilled transliteration/translation approved by the notary and lodged with the foundation charter.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A formal rejection notice is issued by the Registro Público. Within five business days of the notice, the applicant may file a written appeal (recurso de apelación/reconsideración) before the Director General of the Registro Público. The appeal must set out the grounds of eligibility and propose corrective amendments. If the registrar does not issue a confirmation within thirty days, the rejection becomes final, and the applicant may simultaneously submit a new name application. An alternative name can be submitted at any time during the appeal window.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual office arrangements are generally permissible only within a licensed fiduciary or law-firm premises where a dedicated physical desk and file space is allocated to the foundation. A pure mailbox or purely virtual street address without an appointed Panamanian registered agent is not acceptable for bank account opening or AML/CFT compliance.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low quantified risk of approximately 5% annual probability of an unannounced on-site inspection. The probability increases materially where the foundation is flagged for unusual transaction patterns or negative AML screening results; such inspections are conducted by the Registro Público, the Superintendencia de Sujetos No Financieros, or the Unidad de Análisis Financiero.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Name clearance certificate and official registry search
Notarial authorization of foundation charter (Escritura de Constitución)
Foundation registration and inscription fee in the Registro Público
Beneficial ownership filing under Law 23 of 2015 with official certification
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Registro Público de Panamá / Superintendencia de Sujetos No Financieros

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered Panamanian agent and registered office fee, first year

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Ley No. 25 de 12 de junio de 1995 (Ley de Fundaciones de Interés Privado), as amended by Ley No. 8 de 2017 on international fiscal transparency; applicable provisions Arts. 1, 5–10, 16 and 28 (charter contents, endowment, registered agent, foundation council); supplemented by the Public Registry regulatory framework (Acuerdo No. 3 de 2014).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registro Público de Panamá – Dirección General, Sección de Fundaciones de Interés Privado (Public Registry of Panama; headquarters, Panama City; submission window for notarized instruments).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Escritura Pública de Constitución de Fundación de Interés Privado (Foundation Charter Deed), protocolized before a Notary of the Public Circuit of Panama and inscribed in the Foundations Section of the Public Registry.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Law 25/1995 (Private Interest Foundations) mandates a declared initial endowment ('patrimonio inicial') of not less than USD 10,000.00 or its equivalent; no escrow account or bank deposit certification is required at formation. The Founder's declaration in the Foundation Charter suffices; the endowment may be cash, securities or in-kind assets. Registration fee of USD 250.00 is payable to the Public Registry, and the foundation is automatically assigned an RUC upon inscription (Law 8/2017).
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: First Resolution of the Foundation Council: (1) The Foundation Charter and its Regulations are ratified as binding constitutional instruments. (2) The declared initial endowment of USD 10,000.00 is accepted and recorded as the foundation's patrimony. (3) The registered office is fixed at the Resident Agent's address, Panama City, Republic of Panama; the Resident Agent is appointed under Law 25 of 1995. (4) The undersigned Council members are confirmed, and the Chairman and Secretary are elected. (5) The Chairman is authorized to execute banking, contractual, and regulatory filings for the foundation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá – name search window and online certified-agent portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit three proposed foundation names (each ending with 'Fundación' or 'Foundation') in order of priority through a licensed Panamanian attorney or resident agent. The Registry checks conflicting inscriptions and issues a non-certified availability clearance. Reservation is valid for two months; the agent must attach the clearance to the notarial file. A foreign founder must provide an apostilled power of attorney before this step.
required_dossiers: Name availability search application form
Three proposed foundation names in priority order
Founder's passport copy or corporate ID (apostilled/legalized if foreign)
Special power of attorney to the resident agent (apostilled, if executed abroad)
Copy of the resident agent's professional license
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the proposed names are rejected for similarity, the agent immediately submits the next-ranked alternative. A formal reconsideration note (recurso de reconsideración) may be filed within 3 business days, but substitution is the preferred procedural cure to avoid registry delay.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarial Execution of the Foundation Charter
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notaría Pública del Circuito de Panamá (notary of the judicial circuit, Ministry of Government designation)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The Founder or attorney-in-fact appears before the notary and executes the Escritura de Constitución in Spanish. The charter must contain all statutory elements of Law 25/1995: name, registered office, purposes, initial endowment of at least USD 10,000.00, foundation council composition, protector (optional), amendment/dissolution mechanisms, beneficiary and prohibition rules. The notary protocols the instrument and issues certified copies with marginal notarial records.
required_dossiers: Name clearance certificate from the Public Registry
Draft Foundation Charter in Spanish
Founder's passport or corporate documents (apostilled/legalized)
Special power of attorney in favor of the executing attorney, if any
Written acceptance of the Resident Agent
Notarial fee receipt
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary flags drafting defects, a correction instrument (aclaración) is executed before the same notary prior to registry filing; errors detected at this stage incur only notarial correction fees and produce no registry rejection record.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá – Sección de Fundaciones de Interés Privado (tariff cashier and formal submission desk)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The resident agent presents the protocolized Escritura in duplicate, together with the USD 250.00 registration fee receipt and fiscal stamps. The Registry's legal examiners verify compliance with Law 25/1995 and Acuerdo No. 3 de 2014. Upon approval, the Foundation Charter receives a marginal inscription note and the foundation acquires legal personality. The Registry electronically transmits foundation data to the Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) for automatic RUC assignment.
required_dossiers: Protocolized original Foundation Charter with notary's marginal records
Certified duplicate of the Escritura for the Registry archive
Registry tariff payment receipt (USD 250.00)
Paid fiscal stamps (papel sellado/timbres)
Resident agent's submission memorandum
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a defect notice (razón de defecto) is issued, the agent has 30 calendar days to cure by amendment or additional evidence. If the Registry reclassifies the instrument, an appeal (recurso de apelación) may be lodged with the Registry's legal department; no new notarization is required for minor formal omissions.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issuance of Inscription Certificate and Certified Copies
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá – Sección de Fundaciones (certifications and legalization office)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After definitive inscription, the agent requests a 'Certificado de Fundación Inscrita' (personería jurídica) and certified copies of the enrolled charter. Verify the foundation name, date of incorporation, registered office and council members against the registered text. These certified documents form the basis for bank account opening, DGI/NIT confirmation and any municipal licensing.
required_dossiers: Registry inscription receipt (número de ingreso)
Certified-copy request form
Identity document of the requesting attorney or agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the certificate or certified copy contains data errors, request a formal correction via a subsequent note (nota complementaria/subsanación) at the Registry; the wrong metadata does not void the inscription and is cured administratively within 3 business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) – Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas; Municipality of Panama (Alcaldía); and the chosen commercial banking entity
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Confirm the automatic RUC/NIT activation transmitted by the Registry under Law 8/2017; if absent, file the DGI inscription form manually. For bank account opening, present the certified charter, inscription certificate, council resolution and economic activity description (ISIC 6201). If a physical office is maintained, apply for the municipal 'Aviso de Operación/Licencia Comercial'. No national sectoral license applies to cloud software subscription services.
required_dossiers: Certified certificate of inscription (personería jurídica)
Certified copy of the inscribed Foundation Charter
Foundation Council resolution approving banking and tax appointments
Resident agent's certificate of good standing
Confirmation of automatic RUC/NIT activation, or manual DGI application
Economic activity declaration referencing ISIC 6201 / NAICS 511210
Lease agreement or proof of address (only if physical office is opened)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If DGI auto-registration fails or the tax file is queried, a licensed Panamanian accountant files a rectification with a territorial-scope explanation. Municipal license queries are cured by presenting an updated occupancy certificate; any banking declination is remedied by supplementing the council's signature-card resolution.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: No industrial licensing authority is triggered for a cloud software subscription business (ISIC 6201 / NAICS 511210). Service-sector reference authority: Ministerio de Comercio e Industrias (MICI) – Dirección Nacional de Empresas; any municipal 'Aviso de Operación' is administered by the Municipality of Panama (Alcaldía).
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not applicable – remote digital micro-SaaS requires no national operating license. Only if a physical leased office is maintained, a municipal business license ('Aviso de Operación / Licencia Comercial de Negocio') is required; for the foundation itself, the Registry inscription serves as the legal personality document.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministerio de Ambiente (MiAMBIENTE) – Dirección de Evaluación de Impacto Ambiental
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – pure software publishing and subscription services (ISIC 6201) involve no physical works, discharges or land disturbance; EIA Categories I–III under Decreto Ejecutivo No. 123 de 2009 (reglamentario de la Ley 41 de 2001) are not triggered. A home-office or small service office with fewer than 10 employees likewise remains below Category I thresholds.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable for serverless/cloud operations – no on-site wastewater, VOC or combustion emissions. General obligations: municipal solid-waste segregation and collection tariffs; compliance with MiAMBIENTE general noise limits and office sanitation provisions; any office wastewater must meet municipal sewer discharge norms.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: No civil-defense clearance is required for digital-only micro-SaaS operations. If an office is opened: (i) annual fire-safety inspection and certification by the Cuerpo de Bomberos de Panamá; (ii) municipal structural occupancy certificate (permiso de uso) verifying load capacity and egress; and (iii) MITRADEL workplace safety compliance – occupational-risk induction, first-aid equipment and an internal safety handbook. These are administrative self-assessments, not substantive permits.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) del Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas; official portals: www.dgi.gob.pa (Sede Electrónica / Sistema Tributario DGI) for RUC management and filings, and the Facturación Electrónica de Panamá (FEP) platform for digital tax documents.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: The Private Interest Foundation (PIF) is constituted under Ley 25 de 1995 and obtains its juridical personality from the Registro Público de Panamá. For national tax registration: (1) register the foundation charter (Acta Constitutiva) and the appointment of the foundation council with the Public Registry; (2) obtain certified extracts of the Public Registry inscription and valid identity documents / power of attorney of the legal representative; (3) complete the Registro Único de Contribuyente (RUC) application through the DGI's Sistema Tributario portal or at an authorized DGI attention center, submitting the foundation certificate, registered address proof, and representative appointment; (4) upon approval, the PIF is assigned a RUC with an ISR and ITBMS profile. A PIF that will only earn foreign-source SaaS subscription revenue (via Paddle or Lemon Squeezy as Merchant of Record) should register in the non-recurrent / export-services category, indicating no Panamanian-source taxable transactions. Note: the PIF is also liable to the annual Public Registry foundation fee of B/.300 (not an income tax) to remain in good standing.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Territorial_Scope (Panama taxes only Panamanian-source income; the PIF is a separate juridical person subject to entity-level taxation exclusively on Panama-source income, while foreign-source software subscription revenue is outside the Panamanian tax base; no pass-through treatment is available for domestic tax purposes)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Panama has no 'check-the-box' or hybrid mismatch election regime. Available statutory elections include: (a) Régimen Especial de Pequeño Contribuyente for taxpayers with annual gross income up to B/.36,000, replacing full ITBMS filing with a fixed monthly contribution and simplified ISR compliance; (b) voluntary registration as an ITBMS subject even absent Panama-source transactions (useful for zero-rated export invoicing); (c) election to file as a non-recurring exporter with documentary evidence of foreign-source revenue; (d) for larger operations, the Sede de Empresas Multinacionales (SEM) regime — not applicable to a consumer micro-SaaS PIF; the PIF may also request formal written tax consultations (consultas) from the DGI to confirm territorial treatment of specific revenue flows.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (ITBMS - Impuesto de Transferencia de Bienes Muebles y Servicios), Ley 8 de 2010 and subsequent amendments
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: There is no general turnover threshold for ITBMS registration; registration is required from the first taxable transfer of goods or rendering of services sourced in Panama. The special small-taxpayer threshold is B/.36,000 of annual gross income, allowing the simplified fixed-contribution regime instead of full ITBMS compliance. For this PIF, subscription services supplied to foreign end users and settled through foreign Merchant-of-Record platforms (Paddle, Lemon Squeezy) are not Panamanian-source and do not trigger ITBMS registration; if the PIF voluntarily registers, such export transactions must be invoiced at 0%.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory electronic invoicing under the Facturación Electrónica de Panamá (FEP) framework established by Law 256 of 2022, Executive Decree 63 of 2023 and DGI Resolution 201-1129 of 2023. RUC holders are required to issue digitally signed e-invoices, credit/debit notes, final-consumer receipts, and export invoices in XML format, transmit them to the DGI FEP platform, obtain real-time validation, and print the DGI authorization code and QR/digital stamp on each document. Phased implementation applies by taxpayer category, beginning with large taxpayers in 2024 and extending to the remaining RUC population by 2025; deadlines have been periodically adjusted by DGI resolutions. A PIF with exclusively foreign-source revenue and no Panamanian taxable operations is not obliged to operate FEP, but any voluntarily registered zero-rated export invoices must transit the FEP system.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: ITBMS is territorial: services rendered for use, benefit, or economic exploitation outside Panama are zero-rated (0%) under Código Fiscal exemptions for exported services. The consumer micro-SaaS PIF qualifies for 0% on subscription software revenue where (i) the contractual counterparty is the foreign Merchant of Record (Paddle or Lemon Squeezy) or a foreign end client; (ii) the software service is digitally delivered and effectively used/enjoyed outside Panama — server location alone does not create Panamanian nexus; (iii) export invoices are issued at 0% citing the statutory basis; and (iv) consideration is received from abroad into the PIF's bank account. Since the MoR is the seller of record to consumers, the PIF's cross-border flow is a B2B export of services, not a B2C Panama supply. VAT/GST on consumer sales is collected by Paddle/Lemon Squeezy under their own global compliance obligations, with no Panamanian ITBMS liability.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (DUS/Solicitud de Exportación) — required only for physical goods; not applicable to SaaS services
Factura de Exportación / FEP export e-invoice issued at 0% ITBMS with legal basis stated
International service contract between the PIF and the foreign Merchant of Record or end client (Paddle/Lemon Squeezy merchant agreement)
Proof of foreign-source receipt: SWIFT/foreign remittance into the PIF's Panamanian bank account
MoR settlement statements and subscription revenue reports evidencing foreign end-user consumption outside Panama
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: DGI audits export zero-rating on the basis of documentary proof of foreign use/exploitation and receipt of payment from abroad. Failure to substantiate the export triggers reassessment of the 7% ITBMS, late-payment surcharges (recargos) of 5% per month or fraction, up to 100%, plus moratory interest under Código Fiscal Articles 898-904; administrative fines under Article 897 may also apply, including penalties for non-compliant electronic invoicing. Fraudulent zero-rating claims expose the PIF and its representatives to criminal fiscal prosecution (Código Fiscal Articles 939-941) and predicate-offence treatment under the AML framework (Ley 23 de 2015). Documentary records must be retained for at least 5 years, and the DGI assessment window is typically 3 years, extended to 6 where no return is filed and up to 10 in fraud cases. Panama has no exchange-control regime because the US dollar is legal tender; the 180-day benchmark reflects the customs export-liquidation convention for goods and the DGI's evidentiary expectation for crediting export service proceeds. In the MoR model, the PIF should ensure settlement reports and bank inflows are consistent, traced, and archived to withstand clawback scrutiny.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: No central bank exists in Panama. The Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá (SBP) supervises banking, credit, and AML/CFT conduct; the Banco Nacional de Panamá (a state-owned commercial bank) mints fractional Balboa coins and acts as fiscal agent but exercises zero monetary-policy or FX-control authority. The U.S. dollar is legal tender on a full dollarized basis.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full and unrestricted convertibility in both current and capital accounts. The Panamanian Balboa (PAB) is a fixed 1:1 unit of account against the USD and circulates only as fractional coins; the USD is the operative clearing currency. There are no exchange controls, no central-bank approval requirements, and no restrictions on profit remittance or capital repatriation. The only practical friction is standard bank KYC, SBP transaction reporting, and U.S. OFAC screening during USD clearing through U.S. correspondent banks.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None applicable. Panama imposes no surrender, repurchase, conversion, or repatriation timelines on export proceeds, including cross-border SaaS subscription revenue. Exporters and service providers may leave foreign currency offshore, convert it freely, or use it for any lawful purpose without prior notification to the SBP; only standard AML/CTF threshold reports (monthly when cash or cash-equivalent amounts exceed USD 10,000) and the required accounting recognition of the revenue apply.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational USD Account; Capital Escrow Account
Capital Escrow Account; Operational USD Account; Foundation-Asset Custody

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium-High as a settlement-aggregator conduit; Low-Medium as a substitute for a Panamanian bank account. Paddle and Lemon Squeezy are merchant-of-record platforms that lawfully collect and remit SaaS subscription funds; this is the principal inbound settlement rail and is fully compatible with Panamanian law. However, offshore neobank/EMI accounts (e.g., UK FCA- or EU-licensed e-money institutions) are not regulated by the SBP; Panamanian licensed banks treat such EMIs as remittance originators rather than bank reference sources. The PIF should maintain at least one domestic USD operational account as the primary treasury vehicle, use EMIs only as inbound settlement conduits, and avoid permanently parking foundation cash in unaudited e-money wallets. Panama's financial-innovation framework provides a sandbox for licensed payment institutions, but established EMI-native treasury accounts are not yet available.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Most Tier-1 banks require the physical presence of at least one founding Council member or the designated signatory for the onboarding interview; fully remote opening is discretionary and typically granted only to existing clients, high-net-worth referrals, or councils that provide a complete apostilled registration file and undergo a live video compliance interview. A physical signing visit to Panama City remains the safest and fastest route. A general power of attorney is permitted but the Council signatures and source of the initial endowment must still be verified by the compliance officer.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opaque beneficial ownership: a Private Interest Foundation's Charter and by-laws are not publicly registered in the Public Registry, beneficiaries are shielded under Law 25 of 1995, and the bank cannot initially verify ultimate natural-person ownership.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified copy of the Foundation Charter and Articles (apostilled); Registered Agent Certificate of good standing; sworn Beneficiary Register sealed by the Council and Resident Agent; Panamanian counsel legal-opinion letter confirming the lawful commercial purpose; incumbency certificate listing active Council members; and a Foundation resolution authorizing the banking relationship.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Recurring micro-credits from foreign merchant aggregators: the account shows frequent, variable-amount inbound remittances from Paddle.com Market Limited and Lemon Squeezy, which do not conform to a traditional invoice-driven trade pattern.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed Merchant-of-Record agreements with payout schedules; monthly payout statements mapping subscription receipts; a live SaaS dashboard readout; one or more representative consumer subscription agreements; and annual financial statements prepared by a licensed Panamanian accountant.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Capital-injection origin red flag: the USD 10,000 statutory endowment is wired from a founder's personal account or a higher-risk jurisdiction, raising source-of-funds concerns.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Bank statements showing the original funds held at an FCA-, FinCEN-, or EU-licensed institution; founder source-of-wealth letter with supporting tax returns or salary evidence; executed Foundation contributions resolution; and a chain-of-funds diagram prepared by a qualified financial advisor.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Substance mismatch: a micro-SaaS with global subscription revenue, minimal physical footprint, and no visible Panamanian employees is treated as a shell-company matrix.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Third-party cloud service contracts (AWS, Google Cloud); SaaS affiliate or sub-licensing agreements with operating entities; service contracts with Paddle and Lemon Squeezy; registered-office evidence, even if virtual through the Resident Agent; and optional contractor agreements demonstrating real economic activity in Panama's territorial-tax jurisdiction.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The founder instructs its originating bank to send SWIFT MT103 in USD to the PIF's Panamanian account at Banco General or Towerbank; the message travels first to the Panamanian bank's U.S. correspondent (e.g., JPMorgan Chase or BNY Mellon) and then clears over Fedwire/CHIPS into the Panama book-entry account. No exchange-control approval is required because the Balboa is USD-equivalent. Field 70 should read 'PRIVATE INTEREST FOUNDATION CAPITAL CONTRIBUTION PER LAW 25 OF 1995 - SAAS TECHNOLOGY BUSINESS' and field 50K must reference the regulated originator institution. The bank will reconcile the wired amount against the signed contribution resolution and the Foundation's general ledger. For ongoing SaaS income, Paddle and Lemon Squeezy remit monthly merchant-of-record payouts to the same account via SWIFT MT103 with a commercial descriptor; the aggregator dashboard serves as the supporting invoice register.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Payments to vendors, cloud providers, contractors, and tax authorities are executed as SWIFT MT103 from the Panama operational account; SWIFT MT202 cover payments are used when the receiving bank requires a separate cover leg. For U.S.-domiciled contractors, the efficient compliant route is MT103 through the bank's U.S. correspondent, which converts to ACH or Fedwire at the receiving U.S. bank. Commercial Letters of Credit are unsuitable for consumer Micro-SaaS as no shipping documents exist; a Standby Letter of Credit may be used only for enterprise performance guarantees, with the merchant-of-record settlement rails remaining the core collection mechanism. Monthly Paddle and Lemon Squeezy payouts arrive automatically, and manual SWIFT disbursements handle subsequent treasury allocation.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: USD/EUR over-the-counter FX forwards with SBP-licensed banks (Banco General, Towerbank International, Multibank)
USD/EUR European-style FX options with SBP-licensed local counterparties or approved international hedge providers
Cross-currency swaps (USD/EUR) documented under an ISDA Master Agreement with a licensed bank where the PIF has netting capacity
Plain-vanilla FX swaps for operational liquidity between USD and EUR, CAD, or AUD
Non-deliverable forwards on exotic pairs (e.g., COP/CLP) when offered by an SBP-licensed bank; NDFs on USD/Balboa pairs are unnecessary due to full convertibility

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Foundation Franchise Tax Payment (Impuesto Anual de Fundaciones)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas, via authorized Panamanian banks
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually on or before June 30; the tax becomes due on June 1 and a 10% statutory surcharge applies to payments made from July 1 through August 31
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: 10% surcharge for July-August payments; thereafter interest and fines accrue under the Tax Code, and continued non-payment ultimately results in administrative strike-off of the Foundation from the Public Registry

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Final Beneficial Owner Registry Filing and Annual Confirmation (Registro de Beneficiarios Finales)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección Nacional de Registro de Beneficiarios Finales (DNRBF), Registro Público de Panamá, filed through the Foundation's Registered Agent
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Initial filing within 30 days of incorporation; any change in beneficial ownership or control must be filed within 30 days; the Registered Agent must annually verify the continuing accuracy of the filed beneficial ownership record
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Law 254 of 2021 sanctions: monetary fines from B/.1,000 to B/.10,000, suspension of the entity's legal standing, unenforceability of transactions, and possible administrative dissolution for persistent non-compliance

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Continuity of Panama Registered Agent and Registered Office Mandate (Agente Residente)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registro Público de Panamá (Public Registry, through the current registered agent)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Continuous statutory obligation from incorporation; renewed on the Foundation's anniversary; if the agent resigns or is replaced, a new resident agent must be appointed within 30 days
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: No resident agent or registered office is a direct violation of Law 25 of 1995 that can lead to administrative strike-off; acts executed without an active registered agent are denied legal effect and the Foundation loses standing in Panamanian courts

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No compulsory independent audit applies to Private Interest Foundations under Law 25 of 1995. A statutory audit is triggered only if the Foundation earns Panamanian-source gross income at or above the DGI audit benchmark of approximately US$3,000,000 per fiscal year (or holds total assets above US$5,000,000), or if the Foundation Council voluntarily appoints an auditor. Consumer Micro-SaaS subscription revenue collected abroad through Paddle or Lemon Squeezy is foreign-source income and does not trigger mandatory audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Books must be kept in U.S. dollars (Panamanian balboa at par), in accordance with International Financial Reporting Standards as adopted in Panama (NIF), with simplified IFRS for SMEs permitted; financial statements are not publicly filed.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Beneficial ownership information of the PIF is confidential and not recorded publicly. The Foundation Council discloses the beneficiaries and final beneficial owner to the Registered Agent, who files the DNRBF record within 30 days of incorporation and updates it within 30 days of any adjustment to the beneficiary schedule or to the Foundation Council composition. The Registered Agent must annually confirm the accuracy of the DNRBF record and retain the private Register of Beneficiaries at the Panama office.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Beneficiaries (Registro de Beneficiarios, held by the Resident Agent)
Foundation Council Minute Book (Libro de Actas del Consejo de la Fundación)
Accounting Books and Register of Contributed Assets (Libros de Contabilidad y Registro de Bienes)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: US$350 - US$850 per annum for a licensed resident agent, registered office, and basic corporate secretarial services
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: US$1,200 - US$3,500 for a voluntary audit or agreed-upon procedures review by a Panamanian CPA firm

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Panama operates a territorial tax system; foreign-source income is outside the scope of Panamanian corporate income tax. For Panama-source SaaS revenue attributable to a Panama entity, the standard 25% rate applies. Preferential regimes such as SEM (Multinational Headquarters) and Panama-Pacifico licenses are not applicable to a micro SaaS operator without a special license. No statutory tax holiday is available for ordinary software subscription activity.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Declaración de Renta para Personas Jurídicas - Formulario 21 (F-21); filed electronically through the Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) E-tax 6.0 platform.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The return must be filed no later than the last business day of the third month following the fiscal year-end. For a calendar-year taxpayer the deadline is March 31 of the following year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax identification number (Registro Único Contribuyente) of the legal entity.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the Panama RUC assigned to the Private Interest Foundation or its local corporate representative; a foreign tax identification number is not acceptable unless a Panama RUC has been obtained.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax period for which the return is filed.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the fiscal year-end stated in the foundation's charter or, absent such specification, December 31. Quarterly prepayments may be required only if the entity is designated a large taxpayer by the DGI.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross Panama-source revenue before deductions, including software subscription income attributable to activities performed in Panama.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign-sourced SaaS subscription proceeds are excluded from gross revenue if no Panama permanent establishment is maintained; only revenue from Panamanian customers or services rendered from Panama is reportable.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Costs and expenses directly attributable to earning Panama-source income, supported by invoices, receipts, and employment records.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Expenses claimed must be allocable to the Panama-source revenue and substantiated with contemporaneous documentation. Home-office and centralized support costs may be apportioned under a consistent methodology.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net taxable income after expenses allowable under the Panama Fiscal Code.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only net income from Panama sources is treated as taxable; losses connected to foreign sources may not be offset against Panama-source income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax computed at 25% of net taxable income, less advance tax credits and payments already made.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident entities must remit the same 25% statutory rate on Panama-source income; no automatic reduced rate applies without treaty relief.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 60 - Saldo a Favor / A Pagar
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Final assessed tax due after credits, or the carryforward refund balance.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Any balance due must be paid through the DGI fee account before the deadline. Overpayments may be applied to future periods or administratively refunded.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing attracts a surcharge of 2.0% per month or fraction of the tax due, capped at 50% of the tax. Failure to file may also trigger administrative fines of up to USD 5,000, suspension of the Paz y Salvo certificate, and blockage of bank transfers and notarial acts.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Panama has a limited network of income tax treaties. To invoke treaty relief, the non-resident shareholder must be a tax resident of a jurisdiction with an effective DTA and must obtain a Certificate of Tax Residence (TRC) from the competent foreign tax authority. The Panamanian payer must submit the TRC together with the DGI treaty relief application before the dividend distribution is made. Withholding at the reduced treaty rate is permitted only after DGI acceptance; otherwise the 10% statutory rate applies to gross Panama-source dividend distributions to non-resident shareholders.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Panama-source interest paid to non-resident lenders is generally subject to a 10% withholding tax. Interest paid to foreign banking institutions on bona fide market-rate credit is exempt from Panama withholding. Royalties paid to non-residents for the use of software intellectual property in Panama are subject to a 15% statutory withholding tax. DTA rates may reduce these figures where a treaty is in force; otherwise the statutory rates are final.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: B/. 2,500,000 (USD 2.5 million) of annual gross revenue, or B/. 750,000 (USD 750,000) of cross-border related-party transactions, triggers mandatory Local File preparation. A Master File is required where the multinational group's consolidated gross revenue exceeds B/. 15 million.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Panama enacted Economic Substance Requirements (ESR) under Law 254 of 2021. A Private Interest Foundation engaged in holding intangible assets and invoicing SaaS subscriptions must demonstrate physical management presence in Panama if it claims Panamanian tax residency. Required substance indicators include local board meetings, bank accounts in Panama, accounting records, and compliance files. Non-compliance can result in administrative fines of up to USD 100,000 and removal from the tax register.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Willfully omitting Panama-source SaaS revenue from Formulario 21 by booking all subscription income offshore while maintaining a Panama office, bank account, or local customer base.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Panama Fiscal Code Article 756, criminal tax evasion is punishable with imprisonment of 2 to 5 years, plus a fine equal to 100% of the evaded tax. Civil liability includes full back tax, a monthly surcharge of 2%, and default interest of 0.9% per month.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign false returns or direct the evasion can be held personally liable for restitution. Criminal liability extends to officeholders; foreign residents may face Interpol red-flag proceedings, travel bans, and extradition upon issuance of a Panama arrest warrant.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining a Private Interest Foundation with no physical office, no local management, and artificial related-party pricing to shift profits outside Panama while claiming Panamanian tax residency.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: ESR Law 254 of 2021 imposes administrative penalties of USD 5,000 to USD 100,000 for non-compliant entities. The tax administration may also disregard the foundation's separate legal personality for tax purposes and recalculate income at arm's length.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and foundation council members may be jointly and severally liable for unpaid corporate tax, penalties, and costs where the foundation is deemed a shell. In aggravated cases, a director may face disqualification from serving as a company officer and imprisonment of up to 3 years for fraudulent insolvency arising from deliberately unpaid assessed tax.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the micro SaaS payment rails (Paddle, Lemon Squeezy) to channel undisclosed third-party receivables through the Panama entity without an anti-money laundering compliance program, customer due diligence, or suspicious transaction reporting.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Panama's Law 23 of 2015, as reformed, criminalizes money laundering with penalties of 5 to 10 years of imprisonment and fines of B/. 1 million to B/. 5 million for predicate offenses. Financial regulators may also impose administrative penalties on the entity of up to B/. 10 million.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are personally liable for failing to file Suspicious Activity Reports with the Financial Analysis Unit (UAF). Personal exposure includes asset forfeiture, travel restriction orders, and criminal conviction resulting in incarceration. CFO and COO officers who knowingly process flagged payments face both criminal and civil penalties.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Entering into cross-border related-party transactions, such as payments to an affiliate in a no-tax jurisdiction, without a functional and risk analysis or without maintaining a Local File when the threshold is exceeded.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Panama's transfer pricing regime permits the DGI to make primary or secondary adjustments and imposes a 35% penalty on the understated tax, plus interest. Large taxpayers may be automatically escalated to the DGI specialized audit division.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly prepare or rely on fabricated transfer pricing documentation may be charged with complicity in tax evasion, rendering them personally liable for adjusted tax and subject to director disqualification orders from the Registro Público.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Filing Formulario 21 after the statutory deadline or submitting materially incorrect data in the gross-revenue boxes without timely voluntary correction.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Late filing triggers a monthly surcharge of 2% of the tax due, capped at 50%. Submission of false statements carries a fine of USD 1,000 to USD 10,000 in addition to criminal sanctions for making false declarations before the tax administration.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The responsible officer signing the return may be subject to personal fines and, where the false statement conceals tax evasion, a prison term of 2 to 5 years. Travel bans may be issued to secure the presence of the individual for investigation.
